payload.title: The baseline-exam is documented as read-only ('nothing is written', 'writes nothing else', 'nothing written but --out'), but a corrupt runs.jsonl row makes the strict reader append a diagnostic to <store>/diagnostics/ledger-corruption.jsonl, so the exam changes the kept store it is meant to leave identical
evidence: tools/aria-acceptance/harness.py:722 (read_runs_rows is called with base_dir=root, the kept store)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/strict_jsonl_reader.py:85-106 (a corrupt line emits ledger_row_corrupt before the strict raise)
tools/aria-acceptance/harness.py:815-820 (baseline_exam docstring: offline and read-only, nothing is written)
tools/aria-acceptance/harness.py:864-867 (the command docstring: writes nothing else)
payload.rule_violated: F1.3 contract: the exam reads a kept store and leaves it byte-identical; a documented read-only command must not write into the store it reads.
payload.notes: A torn last line in runs.jsonl (a crash while the store was being written) is enough: the exam exits 2 with strict_jsonl_row_corrupt, but before raising the reader creates diagnostics/ledger-corruption.jsonl inside the kept store. The store's fingerprint then differs before and after the exam, a later run of the same exam sees a different store, and the three statements that the command writes nothing are false for exactly the input where an operator is most likely to be checking the store. The evidence reviewer reproduced the new file on a store copy; the store hash was identical for every success and named refusal that does not read a corrupt row. Close condition: Give the strict reader a no-emit mode (or route the diagnostic to stderr when the caller declares a read-only store) and use it from the exam, or verify the ledger with a loader that does not write. Add a test: append a torn line to a store copy, assert exit 2 and that the store's file listing and hashes are unchanged. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
